input:
It is important to note that the defect-reduction project on the packing line has delivered a meaningful improvement in quality performance over the course of one quarter. Specifically, the reject rate decreased from 3.4% to 1.9%, which represents a reduction of 1.5 percentage points. At the current volume of 322k units per year, this improvement avoids about 4830 rejected units per year, underscoring the tangible operational benefit of the project. The result is based on one quarter of production on the packing line, and it is worth noting that the quarter included a planned shutdown; the rates have not been adjusted for the shutdown.

In practical terms, a reject rate reflects the share of units that the line rejects, with the denominator being the production of the line over the period that is measured. The decrease of 1.5 percentage points therefore represents a change in the share itself, stated on the same denominator in both quarters of the comparison. The avoided units are stated at the current annual volume of 322k units, and any future change in volume would move the avoided count in proportion, while the measured rates themselves would stand as recorded. Expressed at the annual volume, the decrease corresponds to the stated figure of 4830 avoided units per year.

The shutdown caveat is also important to keep in mind, and it cuts into the finding in one direction only. Rates measured over a quarter that included a planned shutdown may not fully represent a full quarter of normal running, and no adjustment has been made in order to account for this. Overall, the headline finding for the quarter is the rate decrease from 3.4% to 1.9%; the annual figure essentially restates the same decrease at the annual volume and does not add any new measurement. Going forward, a full-year rate, measured over quarters without a planned shutdown, will be the figure that confirms whether the decrease truly holds over the longer term.
